Duplicate alerts caused by webhook retry storm during Sunday's deploy; added idempotency key check on billing alert creation.

tools.description: List incidents, filterable by status, service, urgency, and created-at date range (GET /incidents)

status.description: Return only incidents with this status. One of: triggered, acknowledged, resolved. Scalar form of the API's statuses[] filter.

service_id.description: Return only incidents associated with this service. Scalar form of the API's service_ids[] filter.

urgency.description: Return only incidents with this urgency. One of: high, low. Scalar form of the API's urgencies[] filter.

since.description: The start of the date range over which you want to search, ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z). Compared against created_at.

until.description: The end of the date range over which you want to search, ISO 8601. Compared against created_at.

limit.description: The number of results per page. Defaults to 30.

tools.name: pd_incident_create
tools.description: Create an incident on a service; auto-assigns the level-1 on-call of the escalation policy when no assignee is given (POST /incidents)

title.description: A succinct description of the nature, symptoms, cause, or effect of the incident (incident.title).

service_id.description: The ID of the service the incident belongs to (incident.service.id).

urgency.description: The urgency of the incident: high or low. Defaults to high (incident.urgency).

details.description: Additional incident details — the body of the incident (incident.body.details).

escalation_policy_id.description: Delegate the incident to this escalation policy instead of the service's default (incident.escalation_policy.id).

priority_id.description: The ID of the priority to set on the incident, e.g. PPRI001 for P1 (incident.priority.id).

assignee.description: User ID to assign the incident to directly (incident.assignments[].assignee.id). If omitted, the level-1 on-call for the escalation policy is assigned.

tools.name: pd_incident_manage
tools.description: Acknowledge, resolve, or escalate an incident; resolving stamps resolved_at, escalating reassigns to the on-call at the given level and re-triggers (PUT /incidents/{id})

id.description: The ID of the incident to manage.

status.description: The new status of the incident: acknowledged or resolved (incident.status). Resolving stamps resolved_at; resolved incidents cannot be modified further.

escalation_level.description: Escalate the incident to the on-call target at this level of its escalation policy; the incident returns to the triggered state (escalation_level).

resolution.description: The resolution message for the incident; recorded as an incident note when status is resolved (incident.resolution).

from.description: The email address of a valid PagerDuty user making the request; maps to the API's required From header and is recorded on log entries.

tools.custom_source:
def pd_oncalls_list(db_path='state.db', **kwargs):
    import sqlite3
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    where = []
    args = []
    for param, column in (('schedule_id', 'o.schedule_id'), ('escalation_policy_id', 'o.escalation_policy_id'), ('user_id', 'o.user_id')):
        value = kwargs.get(param)
        if value:
            where.append(column + ' = ?')
            args.append(value)
    try:
        limit = int(kwargs.get('limit') or 30)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        limit = 30
    sql = ('SELECT o.id, o.escalation_policy_id, ep.name AS escalation_policy_name, '
           'o.schedule_id, s.name AS schedule_name, o.user_id, u.name AS user_name, '
           'u.email AS user_email, o.escalation_level, o.start, o.end_time AS "end" '
           'FROM pd_oncalls o '
           'LEFT JOIN pd_users u ON u.id = o.user_id '
           'LEFT JOIN pd_schedules s ON s.id = o.schedule_id '
           'LEFT JOIN pd_escalation_policies ep ON ep.id = o.escalation_policy_id')
    if where:
        sql += ' WHERE ' + ' AND '.join(where)
    sql += ' ORDER BY o.escalation_policy_id, o.escalation_level LIMIT ?'
    args.append(limit)
    rows = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(sql, args).fetchall()]
    conn.close()
    return {'oncalls': rows, 'total': len(rows)}
